title: sign(): extra CRLF appended to content_mime becomes part of signed content
description:
In sign(), line 186 appends b"
" after content_mime before the boundary delimiter. This extra CRLF (the 'transport padding' or 'encapsulation boundary') is NOT part of what was signed — sign() hashes content_mime directly (line 80). But when verify() is called, the caller must know to extract exactly content_mime bytes (without the trailing 
). The round-trip test (Test E) works because it uses part1.header_range start to body_range end — but this extraction may or may not include the trailing 
 depending on what mail-parser records as the body boundary. If a conformant MUA provides the signed bytes *including* the trailing CRLF transport padding, verify() will fail because the digest won't match. RFC 2046 §5.1.1 and RFC 5751 §3.5 distinguish between the body part bytes and the encapsulation boundary; the CRLF before -- is encapsulation padding, not part of the body. This is worth verifying against an OpenSSL-signed round trip.
notes: INVESTIGATED: Design is correct. sign() appends '\r\n' after content_mime which serves as the RFC 2046 encapsulation boundary CRLF. This CRLF is 'consumed' by the boundary delimiter and is NOT part of the signed content. mail-parser's body_range for part1 ends at the content_mime bytes (excluding the encapsulation CRLF). The sign→verify round-trip test confirms this. NOT a bug.
